correctness.rationale: For fixed \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), all four printed shares are nonnegative and their sum is identically one for every \((\alpha_1,\alpha_2)\in[0,1]^2\). The reported coordinates satisfy \(0.6242+0.8157=1.4399\), so they are valid under the share map but excluded by the later triangle. On the square, every point has objective at least the maximum of the two coordinatewise minima, and choosing independent minimizers attains that lower bound. Fresh exact-rational replay verifies the numerical witness; the universal identities are symbolic.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper itself supplies the inconsistent statements: its four nested shares already exhaust one resource pool for every independent pair of within-stratum splits, yet it later imposes a triangle and then reports a numerical policy outside that triangle. Broader epidemic-allocation literature does not imply this source-specific correction, and targeted exact-ratio and correction searches found no prior correction. The finding is therefore best-of-knowledge original as a diagnosis of this model, not as a new theorem about simplices.
residual_risks: The authors may have intended the later \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\) to denote different top-level shares despite reusing the symbols; that reading would require changing the adjacent allocation formulas and does not match the reported within-stratum ratios.

final_claim: Under the resource-share parameterization printed in the 2026 epidemic-allocation paper, the feasible set for the two within-stratum split variables is the full square \([0,1]^2\), not the later triangle \(\alpha_1+\alpha_2\le 1\); the paper's own Wuhan pair lies outside that triangle, and on the corrected square the instantaneous max objective decouples into the maximum of the two one-dimensional minima.
limitations: The correction is confined to the allocation layer and instantaneous objective.
It does not re-estimate epidemiological parameters or prove a globally optimal dynamic policy when \(\sigma\) is endogenous.
